metadata.notes: Reconstructed buildings stand on the built part of their parcel as Vasserot's block atlas draws it (a traced sheet first, the whole parcel where the atlas says nothing) and have estimated heights. On the Cité each disappears in the year of the works that removed it (until, with until_basis and until_note; see clearances); elsewhere, and where no source dates a house, in 1860 (until_basis: default). Later buildings appear from their APUR construction period.

clearances.note: The east side of the place Dauphine (the even side of the rue de Harlay) burned in the fighting of the Commune in 1871 and was demolished in 1874 to open the view of Duc's new front of the Palais.

The rue d'Arcole was moved east by the decree of 22 May 1865, and every house on both sides came down: from the parvis to the rue de Constantine in November-December 1865, on to the quai in April-June 1866. Marville photographed the old street from the parvis before (Paris Musées 320002473). The street's first widening in 1837 is not modelled: the houses it cut back stand here until 1866 too.
clearances.source: vergue.com, Rue d'Arcole, after the city's records; French Wikipedia, Rue d'Arcole; decree of 22 May 1865 (Ville de Paris street names, record 9034)

clearances.note: On the north edge of the new Hôtel-Dieu's site the houses came down in 1866-1867: the south side of the rue du Haut-Moulin in May-July 1866, its north side and the east side of the rue de la Cité north of the rue de Constantine in April-May 1867. The two sides are not told apart here, so all stand until 1867.
clearances.source: vergue.com, Rue du Haut-Moulin and Rue de la Cité, after the city's records

clearances.note: Razed for the new Hôtel-Dieu (public utility declared 22 May 1865, built 1866-1877). The houses on its site came down from November 1865 to May 1867, most of them in 1866: the rue Saint-Christophe, the rue des Trois-Canettes and the rue de la Licorne first, then the rue de Glatigny, the Ursins streets and the rue Saint-Landry.
clearances.source: vergue.com, Rue Saint-Christophe, Rue des Trois-Canettes and Rue de la Cité, after the city's records; French Wikipedia, Hôtel-Dieu de Paris

clearances.note: The rue Neuve-Notre-Dame and what was left of the rue Saint-Christophe were taken into the enlarged parvis about 1874, the year the old foundlings' hospital on the parvis was pulled down (May 1874). The houses may have gone earlier: no source gives their own year.
clearances.source: Ville de Paris street names, record 14990 (place Jean-Paul-II); French Wikipedia, Parvis Notre-Dame - place Jean-Paul-II, after Le Monde illustré, 6 June 1874

clearances.note: Razed in 1862 for the Cité barracks (decree of 8 August 1860, built 1863-1867), now the Préfecture de police.
clearances.source: vergue.com, Rue de Constantine, after the city's records; Ville de Paris street names, record 15245; French Wikipedia, Préfecture de police (Paris)

clearances.note: The rue aux Fèves, the rue de la Calandre, the rue Saint-Éloi and the rue des Cargaisons were razed in 1862 for the Cité barracks (decree of 8 August 1860), now the Préfecture de police.
clearances.source: vergue.com, Rue de Constantine, after the city's records; Ville de Paris street names, record 15245

clearances.note: Razed in April-July 1866 for the flower market: the rue Gervais-Laurent, the rue Sainte-Croix and what was left of the rue de la Pelleterie.
clearances.source: French Wikipedia, Marché aux fleurs Reine-Elizabeth-II and Rue Gervais-Laurent; vergue.com, Rue Gervais-Laurent and Rue Sainte-Croix, after the city's records

clearances.note: Razed in 1858-1859 for the Tribunal de commerce (built 1860-1865); the bal du Prado, at the corner of the rue de la Pelleterie and the rue de la Barillerie, went in 1858.
clearances.source: vergue.com, Rue de Constantine in 1865, after the city's records; French Wikipedia, Tribunal de commerce de Paris

clearances.note: Under today's street beside the new Hôtel-Dieu: most likely razed with the houses on its site, in 1865-1866. The year is reasoned from those works.
clearances.source: vergue.com, Rue de la Cité and Rue du Cloître-Notre-Dame, after the city's records

clearances.note: Under today's street beside the Cité barracks (now the Préfecture de police): most likely razed with the houses on its site in 1862. The year is reasoned from those works.
clearances.source: vergue.com, Rue de Constantine, after the city's records

clearances.note: Under today's street beside the flower market: most likely razed with the houses on its site in 1866. The year is reasoned from those works.
clearances.source: French Wikipedia, Marché aux fleurs Reine-Elizabeth-II

clearances.note: Under today's street beside the Tribunal de commerce: most likely razed with the houses on its site in 1858-1859. The year is reasoned from those works.
clearances.source: vergue.com, Rue de Constantine in 1865, after the city's records

clearances.note: Still standing in 1865: Marville photographed it, rue du Cloître-Notre-Dame, seen from the parvis (after 1865; Paris Musées 320002496). The houses in the frame are read from the title.
clearances.source: Charles Marville, rue du Cloître-Notre-Dame, seen from the parvis, after 1865, Musée Carnavalet (Paris Musées 320002496, CC0)

clearances.note: Still standing in 1865: Marville photographed it, rue des Marmousets, seen from the rue Saint-Landry (between 1865 and 1868; Paris Musées 320002470). The houses in the frame are read from the title.
clearances.source: Charles Marville, rue des Marmousets, seen from the rue Saint-Landry, between 1865 and 1868, Musée Carnavalet (Paris Musées 320002470, CC0)

clearances.note: Still standing in 1865: Marville photographed it, rue Basse-des-Ursins (between 1865 and 1868; Paris Musées 320002475). The houses in the frame are read from the title.
clearances.source: Charles Marville, rue Basse-des-Ursins, between 1865 and 1868, Musée Carnavalet (Paris Musées 320002475, CC0)

clearances.note: Still standing in 1865: Marville photographed it, rue de la Colombe, seen from the quai (between 1865 and 1868; Paris Musées 320002476). The houses in the frame are read from the title.
clearances.source: Charles Marville, rue de la Colombe, seen from the quai, between 1865 and 1868, Musée Carnavalet (Paris Musées 320002476, CC0)

clearances.note: Still standing in 1865: Marville photographed it, rue Chanoinesse, seen from the rue des Chantres (between 1865 and 1868; Paris Musées 320002499). The houses in the frame are read from the title.
clearances.source: Charles Marville, rue Chanoinesse, seen from the rue des Chantres, between 1865 and 1868, Musée Carnavalet (Paris Musées 320002499, CC0)
